metadata.title: Swallowing Hermès: Family Feuds, Century Capital Wars, and €10B Shares That Vanished

conclusion: Hermès heir Nicholas Puech alleges ~6M shares (~€10B) vanished via advisor Eric Freymond, pulling LVMH/Arnault into court. The episode braids a personal fraud tale — gardener family, forged transfers, Freymond's Alpine death — into Arnault's decade-long stealth accumulation through equity swaps with Natixis/SocGen/Amundi below disclosure thresholds, timed after CEO Dumas's illness. Latest sting: Hermès Q1 sales −1.4%, intraday stock −14%. Owning the bag or the shares both got harder.
background: Luxury soap-opera meets capital markets structure: how cash-settled swaps flipped to physical delivery, how an heir's advisor allegedly fed the float, and why family control myths meet activist/regulator limits.
important_facts: Framing: Birkin scarcity culture vs family absurdity — 6M Hermès shares (~€10B; '200+ high-speed train cars of Birkins') disappear from fifth-generation heir Nicholas Puech. He sues ex-advisor Freymond and LVMH/Arnault (May prior year), suspecting a setup despite little operational overlap between houses.

Personal thread: pandemic-era gardener household gifted 50+ properties; gardener's wife catches Freymond lying about a CHF1M transfer → audit → missing shares. Freymond accused of aggravated breach of trust; accounts/art frozen; dies by train near Swiss chalet two weeks after questioning (ruled suicide). Probe: 2001 LVMH Geneva contact; 2008 ~4.8M shares into Dilico then SocGen swap leg at ~€86.66 vs >€1600 now.

Macro war: Arnault builds stake via three banks — Natixis ~5.0M (4.7%), SocGen ~4.8M (4.5%), Amundi ~3.2M (3.0%) — each under banner thresholds; switches cash settlement to physical after June 2010 when legendary CEO Dumas is terminally ill. Oct 23, 2010 disclosure shock. Coda: Apr 15 print Q1 sales €4.07B (−1.4%) and −14% intraday crash — largest in Hermès history cited.

mental_model.name: Family Custody Risk × Stealth Swap Accumulation × Brand Multiple Fragility
mental_model.components: Separate heir operational security from brand mystique; map equity-swap scaffolding that stays under 5% prints; remember luxury multiples still reprice on growth misses.
mental_model.application: RMS longs need governance/float literacy, not only Birkin waitlists. MC/LVMH history shows multi-year optionality on family disputes. Event risk around French luxury earnings remains fat-tailed.

key_insights.view: The vanished block is both crime story and float story.
key_insights.question: How do €10B shares go quiet?
key_insights.answer: Trusted advisor + opaque entities + swap plumbing — not a single exchange print.

key_insights.question: Why three banks?
key_insights.answer: Keep each sleeve under disclosure thresholds until physical settlement at Hermès's weakest hour.

key_insights.view: Even Hermès equity is not a platinum bag.
key_insights.question: What's the 2026 sting?
key_insights.answer: Q1 miss triggered a record intraday −14% — scarcity branding ≠ earnings immunity.

Historical stealth accumulation shows Arnault's optionality on Hermès drama; legal overhang cuts both ways — low
